svg.title: cipher wheel · guide
svg.text: How the wheel works
1. Pin the inner disk on the outer disk through both centres.
2. Turn the inner disk until the card's key number sits under the red mark.
3. For each character on the card, find it on the inner disk and write down the outer letter next to it.
“_” is a space. Space, comma and period are letters like any other, so the card hides even where words end.
Why every reply fits
The Library of Babel has 29 characters: a to z, space, comma, period. Before a reply goes on a card, it's
written in that alphabet, so the same wheel decodes any reply the model writes:
capitals → lowercase
? and ! → a period
: and ; → a comma
digits → spelled out (24 → twenty four)
line breaks, dashes, slashes → a space
everything else → dropped (quotes, apostrophes, stars…)
What the key is, and isn't
A key is one setting out of 29: 4.86 bits. A reply of 70 characters costs 340 bits in Babel. The key doesn't
find the reply; the reply is already on the card. Try the wrong key and you get readable-looking noise that costs
exactly as much in Babel. Nothing on the wheel marks the right key. You know it's right because it reads as
language, and that sense comes from reading: from the weighting. The visitor plays the model.
Making cards
Any reply on the whose-words page: “print as a Babel card” under the reply. Any text:
uv run python physical/cipher_wheel.py card --text "…" --key 18
